pool.prompt: Two technicians are both working on a locked-out equipment rack. One applies a lock. Under 29 CFR 1910.147(f)(3), what must the second technician do?
choices: Rely on the first technician's lock — only one lock per equipment item is needed
Apply their own separate padlock to a group lockout hasp on the same energy isolating device
Apply a tagout tag because only one lock is allowed per hasp
Notify the supervisor and wait outside the work area
pool.explanation: Per 29 CFR 1910.147(f)(3), in a group lockout each authorized employee must apply their own personal padlock to a group lockout hasp. The equipment cannot be re-energized until every worker has removed their own lock — one worker's lock protects only that worker.

pool.prompt: What is the physical device (breaker, valve, disconnect switch) that a lock or tag is applied to during a LOTO procedure called?
choices: The energy isolating device
The equipment rack
The service panel
The safety interlock
pool.explanation: The energy isolating device (EID) is the mechanism that physically prevents energy from flowing to the equipment being serviced. The lock is applied to the EID — not to the equipment itself — because the EID is the control point where energy can actually be blocked.

pool.prompt: A technician is splicing fiber inside a remote fiber hut next to a battery backup rack, doing no work on the rack itself. Does 29 CFR 1910.147 LOTO apply?
choices: Yes — apply LOTO because the fiber splicer uses 120V AC wall power
No — LOTO applies to servicing/maintenance of equipment; fiber splicing in the room isn't servicing the energized racks
Yes — any work in the same room as energized equipment requires LOTO
Yes, but only if the battery rack is within 3 feet of the splice work
pool.explanation: 29 CFR 1910.147 applies to servicing and maintenance of machines and equipment where unexpected energization could injure the worker. Working near — but not servicing — the equipment does not trigger LOTO, though safe work practices near live equipment still apply under 1910.268.

pool.prompt: After completing maintenance work, in what order does re-energization occur under 29 CFR 1910.147(e)?
choices: Remove lock -> restore energy -> clear work area -> notify affected employees
Remove lock -> restore energy -> notify affected employees
Clear work area -> each worker removes own lock -> notify affected employees -> restore energy
Restore energy -> clear work area -> workers retrieve locks -> notify affected employees
pool.explanation: 29 CFR 1910.147(e) requires: (1) remove tools/materials, (2) ensure all employees are clear, (3) each authorized employee removes their own lock, (4) notify affected employees, (5) restore energy. Workers must be clear and notified BEFORE re-energization.

pool.prompt: What is the correct sequence of the six-step LOTO procedure under 29 CFR 1910.147(d)?
choices: Shutdown -> Preparation -> Lockout application -> Isolation -> Verification -> Stored energy release
Preparation -> Shutdown -> Isolation -> Lockout/tagout device application -> Stored energy release/restraint -> Verification of isolation
Isolation -> Preparation -> Shutdown -> Verification -> Stored energy release -> Lockout application
Preparation -> Verification -> Shutdown -> Isolation -> Lockout application -> Stored energy release
pool.explanation: The sequence is: (1) preparation for shutdown, (2) machine/equipment shutdown, (3) isolation, (4) lockout/tagout device application, (5) stored energy release or restraint, (6) verification of isolation (zero-energy check). Verification is the final step and one of the most commonly skipped, most frequently cited failures.

pool.prompt: Why does verification of isolation (the final LOTO step) matter, even after locks have been applied?
choices: It confirms the actual zero-energy state — a lock alone doesn't guarantee the isolating device fully disconnected the energy source; the worker must attempt to restart/test to verify
It is a purely administrative step with no safety function
It replaces the need to apply a lock at all
It is only required when more than one worker is involved
pool.explanation: Verification means the authorized employee attempts to restart the machine (pressing the start button, testing circuits) after applying the lock, to confirm the energy source is actually isolated — a lock on the wrong device, or a device that didn't fully isolate, would otherwise go undetected. This step is one of the most frequently cited LOTO violations when skipped.

pool.prompt: During a group lockout on shared equipment, when can the equipment be re-energized?
choices: As soon as the most senior technician removes their lock
Only after every authorized employee who applied a lock has personally removed their own lock
As soon as the supervisor gives verbal approval, regardless of locks still in place
After a fixed 30-minute waiting period, regardless of lock status
pool.explanation: In a group lockout, each authorized employee's lock protects only that employee. Re-energization cannot occur until every individual lock has been removed by the person who applied it — this ensures no worker is exposed to unexpected energization while still in the work area.

pool.prompt: A technician needs to work on a piece of equipment that has multiple energy sources (electrical AND stored pneumatic pressure). What does step 5 of the LOTO sequence require?
choices: Only the electrical source needs isolation; stored pressure is not covered by LOTO
All stored or residual energy (including pneumatic, hydraulic, spring-loaded, or gravitational) must be released or restrained before work begins
Stored energy release is optional if the equipment has been powered off for more than an hour
Stored energy only needs to be addressed if it exceeds 1,800 lbf
pool.explanation: Step 5 of the LOTO sequence (29 CFR 1910.147(d)(5)) requires release or restraint of ALL stored or residual energy — not just the primary energy source being locked out. Pneumatic, hydraulic, spring-loaded, and gravitational energy can all injure a worker even after the primary electrical source is isolated.
